name: mushroom eggplant ragu
instructions:
A simple sautéed mix of EGGPLANT + MUSHROOMS + ONIONS on a canned-tomato base, tossed with pasta. NO WINE, NO SPICES beyond salt and pepper — the whole point is a simpler, more vegetable-forward alternative to bolognese (bolognese.json). Meat is optional and either type (vegan beef or real beef) works.

SERVES 4.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- pasta (penne, rigatoni, or other short shape)
- 3-4 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 3-4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium EGGPLANT, diced
- 8-10 oz MUSHROOMS (portabella, cremini, or shittake — any work), sliced or diced
- OPTIONAL: 8-12 oz meat — ground vegan beef OR real ground beef (both work; see notes)
- 1 (28-oz) can crushed tomatoes (or whole peeled crushed by hand)
- salt and black pepper to taste

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Cook pasta in well-salted water to al dente. Reserve some pasta water.
2. Heat olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add onion; cook until soft (5-7 min). Add garlic; cook 1 min more.
3. Add EGGPLANT and MUSHROOMS. Sauté over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until both are soft and browned (10-15 min). Don't rush — real color on the eggplant and mushrooms is what carries the flavor.
4. IF USING MEAT: push the vegetables to the side of the pan, add the meat, break it up, and cook until no longer raw (or fully browned if using real beef — either works).
5. Add the canned tomatoes. Simmer 10-15 min to integrate and thicken.
6. Salt and black pepper to taste.
7. Toss with cooked pasta, loosening with reserved pasta water as needed.
notes:
PURPOSE OF THIS RECIPE: a simpler, more vegetable-forward alternative to bolognese (bolognese.json). Key differences: no wine, no spices beyond salt+pepper, no long simmer, no dairy (or minimal), no lentils / walnuts. If you want a bolognese, make a bolognese. This is what to make when you want a straightforward mushroom-eggplant-onion pasta without the bolognese apparatus.

=== NO WINE, NO SPICES ===

No wine (white, red, or vinegar). No spices beyond salt and black pepper. No dried oregano, no red chili flakes, no basil. The dish is deliberately simple — the sautéed vegetables + canned tomato + pasta are the whole thing.

If you find yourself reaching for wine or spices, make bolognese instead (variant A for real beef with white wine + thyme; variant B for lentil + toasted walnut with red wine + oregano + balsamic).

=== MEAT IS OPTIONAL — VEGAN BEEF OR REAL BEEF, EITHER WORKS ===

Meat is optional. When used, either GROUND VEGAN BEEF or REAL GROUND BEEF works — the recipe doesn't lean either direction. The eggplant + mushroom already carry enough meat-analog texture that the choice is more about diet preference than dish structure.

No need to brown real beef hard here (unlike bolognese variant A where Marcella specifically says not to brown) — the sauté approach means everything gets some color together.

=== SAUTÉ HARD ENOUGH TO GET REAL COLOR ===

The eggplant and mushrooms both need to develop real color in the pan for the flavor to work. This isn't a soft-sweat step — cook them over medium-high heat until they're browned and the eggplant is soft all the way through. 10-15 min minimum in the pan. Rushed sauté means the finished dish reads flat.

=== NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES ===

Regular canned crushed tomatoes (or whole peeled crushed by hand). Fire-roasted is the signature of fire-roasted-meatballs.json — using them here reads too smoky against the vegetable base.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- bolognese: the bolognese family (Julia beef; Nisha lentil-walnut). More complex — wine, spices, longer simmer, dairy or dairy-adjacent, potentially lentils/walnuts. Reach for it when you want a proper bolognese; reach for THIS when you want a simpler vegetable-forward pasta.
- fire-roasted-meatballs: same sauté-and-tomato shape but with meatballs + fire-roasted tomatoes + specific italian-american flavor stack.
- tomato pasta sauce family — [[marcella-tomato-sauce]], [[sicilian-pesto-rosso]], [[vodka-sauce]], [[pasta-piperade]], [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]] (all tagged 'tomato pasta sauce'): the protein-free italian pasta-sauce family.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — SIMPLIFIED FROM VEGETABLE-RAGU ===

This file used to be called mushroom-eggplant-ragu.json and had two variants: an eggplant + mushroom + ground vegan meat variant (with red wine vinegar + porcini powder + nutritional yeast), and a mushroom + lentil variant (with red wine + parmesan/nutritional yeast finish). The mushroom-lentil path is deprecated here — lentils belong in bolognese variant B (Nisha's) instead. The eggplant path has been simplified: no wine vinegar, no porcini powder, no nutritional yeast — just the sauté + canned tomato + optional meat.
